issue_context.title: AlgoSeekOptionsConverter 7zip implementation
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
A reliable way to decompress the massive AlgoSeek's OPRA files.

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
The actual implementation relying in `7zip` is very unstable. Given the wide variability in the OPRA file sizes (from 60MB up to +2GB), setting a time out is tricky and it doesn't assure it'll cover all possibilities.

Also sometimes the actual implementation simply throws `7Zip Exited Unsuccessfully`, meaning that the 7zip failed, even before the time out span passes. 

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
One potential solution  is using some C# implementation (like `SharpZipLib`) for decompressing the data, with the limitation that raw data cannot be fully stored in memory.

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->
The error is `7Zip Exited Unsuccessfully` hard to reproduce, given the same OPRA file and hardware sometimes  it fails, sometimes not. 

Also the `time out` error depends on the OPRA file size and the hardware were it is run. In a AWS EC2 `c4.2xlarge` instance, an OPRA file with more than 1GB, throws the error.

#### System Information
<!--- Required for Bugs. Include any system specific information, such as OS. -->
Ubuntu 16, AWS EC2 c4.2xlarge
